title: Turning at the Second Bridge
story: After a month away from running, Yusuf wanted his old route along the canal, which took about forty minutes at an easy pace. His physiotherapist had cleared him to jog, but only if he stopped at the first sharp pain and kept the distance short. He told his friend Farid they would turn at the second bridge, not at the lock where they used to finish. Farid agreed to match that slower plan instead of going ahead. They set off in the cool evening, and Yusuf noticed his calf felt tight but not painful. At the bridge he was tempted to continue, because his breathing felt easy. He remembered the instruction and turned around. The walk back counted as part of the session. At home he wrote the time and the fact that the tight feeling faded after he stretched. He would add a little more next week only if the calf stayed calm.

vocabulary.definition: The speed of a run or a walk.
A specialist who treats joints and muscles with exercise.
The fleshy back of the lower leg.
Strongly drawn towards a choice that may be unwise.
Gently lengthened a muscle after exercise.

quiz.question: Where did the two friends agree to turn?
options: At the second bridge, not at their old finish
At the lock, as they had always done
At home, before they started running
Wherever Yusuf's breathing felt easiest
quiz.correctAnswer: At the second bridge, not at their old finish
quiz.explanation: Yusuf said they would turn at the second bridge, not at the lock where they used to finish.
quiz.supportingSentence: He told his friend Farid they would turn at the second bridge, not at the lock where they used to finish.

quiz.question: What conditions did the physiotherapist set?
options: He could jog, but had to stop for sharp pain and stay short
He had to repeat the full old route that evening
He could run only if Farid went ahead
He was told not to stretch after the run
quiz.correctAnswer: He could jog, but had to stop for sharp pain and stay short
quiz.explanation: He was cleared to jog only if he stopped at the first sharp pain and kept the distance short.
quiz.supportingSentence: His physiotherapist had cleared him to jog, but only if he stopped at the first sharp pain and kept the distance short.

quiz.question: What nearly made Yusuf pass the agreed turning point?
options: His breathing felt easy, so continuing seemed possible
A sharp pain forced him to sprint
Farid refused to turn with him
The specialist was waiting further along the canal
quiz.correctAnswer: His breathing felt easy, so continuing seemed possible
quiz.explanation: He was tempted to continue because his breathing felt easy.
quiz.supportingSentence: At the bridge he was tempted to continue, because his breathing felt easy.

quiz.question: How should the walk back be understood?
options: As part of the training rather than a failed run
As proof that the evening had been wasted
As a race against Farid to the lock
As a reason to skip the notes at home
quiz.correctAnswer: As part of the training rather than a failed run
quiz.explanation: The walk back counted as part of the session, so turning early was still training.
quiz.supportingSentence: The walk back counted as part of the session.

quiz.question: What does tempted mean in this story?
options: Drawn towards an unwise choice
Ordered by a specialist to stop
Told to write the time at home
Matched to a slower friend's plan
quiz.explanation: He was tempted to continue past the plan, so he was drawn towards a choice he should not make.
quiz.supportingSentence: At the bridge he was tempted to continue, because his breathing felt easy.
